study.title: Effects of Long-Term Acupuncture Treatment on Resting-State Brain Activity in Migraine Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial on Active Acupoints and Inactive Acupoints
study.article_type: randomized controlled trial with neuroimaging substudy
study.study_design: single-blind, randomized controlled trial with two groups: active acupuncture group and inactive acupuncture group; resting-state fMRI conducted at baseline and end of treatment in a randomly selected subsample
study.randomization: computerized block-randomization with the SAS procedure PROC PLAN in the SAS package (SAS Version 9.0); block size set to 4, number of blocks was 20; opaque sealed envelopes with consecutive numbers used for allocation concealment
study.blinding: single-blind; two acupuncturists not blinded; investigators in charge of patient screening and randomized distribution knew group assignment but not corresponding treatment schedule; outcome assessor blinded throughout the study; patients blinded to group assignment
study.population: migraineurs without aura enrolled from the neurology department of the Teaching Hospital of Chengdu University of TCM; recruitment June 2012 through March 2013
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) all subjects were right-handed and had 2 to 6 migraine attacks per month during the last 3 months and during the baseline period (4 weeks before enrollment); (2) all subjects were 18 to 55 years of age; in addition, the start of headache needed to be before the age of 50; (3) received education for more than 6 years and completed the baseline headache diary; (4) had not taken any prophylactic headache medicine or any acupuncture treatment during the last 3 months; (5) no record of long-term analgesics consumption; and (6) had no contraindications to exposure to a high magnetic field
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) existence of neurological diseases; (2) hypertension, diabetes mellitus, hypercholesteremia, vascular/heart disease, and major systemic conditions; (3) pregnant or lactating women; (4) alcohol or drug abuse; (5) any neuroimaging research study participation during the last 6 months; and (6) inability to understand the doctor's instructions

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: SJ5: on the dorsal aspect of the forearm on the line connecting SJ4 and the tip of the elbow, 2 cun above the transverse crease of the wrist between the ulna and radius; GB20: in a depression between the upper portion of the sternocleidomastoid muscle and the trapezius; GB34: on the lateral aspect of the lower leg in the depression anterior and inferior to the head of the fibula; GB40: anterior and inferior to the external malleolus in a depression on the lateral side of the tendon of the extensor digitorum longus
interventions.needle_type_exact: single-use stainless steel filiform needles (Hwato Needles, Sino-foreign Joint Venture Suzhou Hua Tuo Medical Instruments Co., China)
interventions.needle_size_exact: 25 mm–40 mm in length and 0.25 mm–0.30 mm in diameter
interventions.manipulation_exact: Needles were twisted with rotation (90°<amplitude<180°) at a frequency of 1–2 Hz. Stimulation was repeated 1–3 times to acquire the de-qi sensation
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: yes; de-qi sensation (soreness, numbness, heaviness, distention and dull pain at the site of needle placement) sought
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: 32 sessions over 8 weeks (once every other day, preferably 4 times a week)
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: two specialized acupuncturists with at least five years of training and three years of experience; received special training prior to the study
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: patients were informed that they would receive one of two types of acupuncture treatment, which depended on different traditional Chinese acupuncture theories
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: active acupoints selected according to traditional classic and systematic reviews of ancient and modern literature of acupuncture for migraine upon several consensus meetings with experts based on the experience from previous study

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: SJ22: on the side of the head on the posterior border of the hairline of the temple at the level with the root of the auricle, posterior to the superficial temporal artery; PC7: in the middle of the transverse crease of the wrist between the tendons of the palmaris longus and flexor carpi radialis; GB37: on the lateral aspect of the lower leg 5 cun above the tip of the external malleolus on the anterior border of the fibula; SP3: proximal and inferior to the head of the 1st metatarsal-phalangeal joint in a depression at the junction of the red and white skin

extraction_notes.note: The paper states coordinates are in Talairach space in Table 3, but MNI template (SPM5) was used for spatial normalization. It is possible that the coordinates were converted from MNI to Talairach prior to reporting, but this conversion is not explicitly described. This should be flagged for coordinate-based neuroimaging synthesis.

Table 3 is split across two PDF pages and rendered via OCR. Some cells appear to be blank or cut off in the inactive group column. Specifically, the MeFG row for the inactive group shows coordinates x=45, y=2, z=44 with t=3.69, BA10, increase, cluster=26 — these coordinates seem unusual for a left medial frontal gyrus structure (x=45 is right hemisphere). This may be an OCR rendering artifact. The t value and cluster size are clearly legible.

extraction_notes.note: The direct between-group comparison (Figure 4) showing higher/lower ReHo in active vs inactive group is presented only as a figure with narrative text. No coordinate table is provided for this contrast. Coordinates are not extractable from the figure.

Figure 5 shows correlation scatter plots. P values visible in figure (p = 0.0020 for ACC group A, p = 0.0003 for insula group A, p = 0.0015 for ACC group B) are reported from the figure caption/axes. The main text reports Bonferroni-corrected P < 0.05 thresholds. These values may differ from or complement the text.
The paper does not report global signal regression status for preprocessing. This is not reported in the methods.
Expectancy was not formally measured. Authors note this as a limitation: 'Lack of an index to access and quantify the expectancy during the acupuncture treatment session is another limitation.'
PMID not reported in the extracted PDF. DOI is 10.1371/journal.pone.0099538.

The paper reports that 80 patients were analyzed by ITT, but 7 dropped out during the study (2 from active, 5 from inactive group). The LOCF method was used for dropouts. The n_analyzed for the fMRI subsample was 20 per group (40 total), all of whom completed fMRI scans.

Table 2 shows baseline VAS score for active fMRI subsample as 5.28 (2.03) and inactive fMRI subsample as 5.44 (1.48), while Table 1 (ITT) shows means of 5.11 (1.75) and 5.23 (1.78) respectively. These differ because Table 2 refers only to the 20-patient fMRI subsamples, while Table 1 refers to the full ITT cohort.
The paper does not report separate follow-up neuroimaging data beyond the 8-week treatment endpoint. No follow-up neuroimaging was conducted.

The right hemisphere hippocampus row in Table 3 for the active acupoint group appears empty/blank in the PDF rendering. Only the left hippocampus decrease is reported in the text (section 3.2) and extractable from the table.
